evidence.quote:
6. Finally, the article, also in Section 2, includes the following quote in the second paragraph:
“Twenty countries, representing approximately 50% of the global population, account for over
80% of the estimated global excess mortality for the January 2020 to December 2021 period.
These countries are Brazil, Colombia, Egypt, Germany, India, Indonesia, the Islamic Republic of
Iran, Italy, Mexico, Nigeria, Pakistan, Peru, the Philippines, Poland, the Russian Federation, South
Africa, the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Turkey, Ukraine, and the United
States of America (USA).”
I do not believe that Nigeria's inclusion among the countries representing 80% of global excess
mortality due to COVID-19 is accurate. Firsthand experience suggests that Nigeria was one of the
African nations that experienced significantly fewer deaths from the virus.

Dear reviewer, Thank you very much for your thorough feedback. Though we understand
that your first-hand experience of Nigeria's excess mortality due to COVID-19
maybe different, the text quoted in our article, in the sub-section 'The emergence of COVID19 in late 2019', is directly from this WHO (2022) article: Global excess deaths associated
with COVID-19: January 2020-December 2021. World Health Organisation. Available from
here: [external resource identifier omitted] We will address the invaluable comments you have made in a
revised version of this paper.
